evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister to arrest a downward economic spiral and restart IMF talks.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new finance minister faces tight time frame to tackle crises
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister to arrest a downward economic spiral and restart IMF talks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous reporting syndicated by Euronews, with direct description of the appointment and task.
evidence.period_fit: April 2022 accession and early stabilization period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Sharif's cabinet choice; later constrained by inherited crisis conditions.
contrary_evidence: The appointment occurred inside a severe economic and coalition crisis.
It did not prevent later cabinet turnover.

evidence.claim: PML-N stalwart Ishaq Dar was nominated by Nawaz Sharif and PM Shehbaz and appointed finance minister after Miftah Ismail resigned, amid internal disagreement over fuel-price decisions.
evidence.title: Ishaq Dar appointed federal finance and revenue minister
evidence.excerpt: PML-N stalwart Ishaq Dar was nominated by Nawaz Sharif and PM Shehbaz and appointed finance minister after Miftah Ismail resigned, amid internal disagreement over fuel-price decisions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with the Cabinet Division notification and named attribution to the PM's advice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's advice and the party leadership's preferences.
contrary_evidence: Dar is a political stalwart rather than a neutral technocrat.
The replacement suggests loyalty politics alongside expertise.

evidence.claim: The government said it would raise taxes on the rich and ban government officials from buying new cars in the 2022/23 budget to reduce the deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.title: Pakistan to raise taxes on rich, ban some car buying to secure IMF bailout
evidence.excerpt: The government said it would raise taxes on the rich and ban government officials from buying new cars in the 2022/23 budget to reduce the deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on an official budget announcement and the policy content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct cabinet policy under Sharif, though prepared through the finance ministry.
contrary_evidence: Mostly a stabilization and austerity measure rather than a growth program.
Immediate burdens rose during a crisis year.

evidence.claim: Finance Minister Miftah Ismail said the government ended fuel subsidies and raised prices to trim the fiscal deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.title: Pakistan further removes fuel subsidies to win IMF funding
evidence.excerpt: Finance Minister Miftah Ismail said the government ended fuel subsidies and raised prices to trim the fiscal deficit and secure IMF support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous report on a directly announced policy shift.
evidence.period_fit: June 2022, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct policy choice under Sharif; it also unwound an inherited subsidy package.
contrary_evidence: The move was inflationary and politically costly.
It mainly reversed a predecessor policy rather than creating new prosperity.

evidence.claim: The State Bank raised the policy rate to 15 percent to control spiraling inflation after a 13-year-high inflation reading.
evidence.title: SBP raises policy rate by 125bps to 15pc
evidence.excerpt: The State Bank raised the policy rate to 15 percent to control spiraling inflation after a 13-year-high inflation reading.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous central-bank reporting in a major Pakistani outlet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: SBP is independent, but the move reflects the macro regime under Sharif's government.
contrary_evidence: Rate hikes show stabilization effort, but also the severity of the macro crisis.
Monetary tightening alone could not offset fiscal and external stress.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Pakistani authorities would establish an electronic asset declaration system and review anticorruption institutions, including NAB, to improve governance.
evidence.title: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on the Combined Seventh and Eight Reviews for Pakistan’s Extended Fund Facility
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Pakistani authorities would establish an electronic asset declaration system and review anticorruption institutions, including NAB, to improve governance.
evidence.source_locator: governance and corruption section near the end of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF statement describing government commitments and reform steps.
evidence.period_fit: July 2022, squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif's administration, though implementation depended on institutions and parliament.
contrary_evidence: Commitments are not the same as enacted reform.
The IMF package also reflected crisis pressure and external conditionality.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities had taken important measures and the immediate priorities were FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, expanded social safety, and SOE governance reform.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Completes the Combined Seventh, and Eighth Reviews of the Extended Fund Facility for Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the authorities had taken important measures and the immediate priorities were FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, expanded social safety, and SOE governance reform.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official board decision and staff appraisal with specific policy priorities and quantified program context.
evidence.period_fit: Late August 2022, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Sharif's government, though much was driven by inherited imbalances and external financing stress.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also said FY22 policy was procyclical and unsustainable.
Corrective action indicates prior mismanagement rather than clean stewardship.

evidence.claim: The World Bank projected only 2 percent growth for FY23, around 23 percent inflation, and a worsening poverty rate because of floods, tight money, high debt, and weak external conditions.
evidence.title: World Bank: Pakistan’s Economy Slows Down While Inflation Rises Amid Catastrophic Floods
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank projected only 2 percent growth for FY23, around 23 percent inflation, and a worsening poverty rate because of floods, tight money, high debt, and weak external conditions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct World Bank update with quantified macro and welfare projections.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly inherited and shock-driven; Sharif’s response mattered in cushioning impact and adjusting policy.
contrary_evidence: The deterioration was heavily driven by floods and global conditions.
This is more an outcome/constraint source than a clean ruler-performance source.

evidence.claim: Sharif said flood relief assistance under BISP would rise from Rs28 billion to Rs70 billion and each affected family would receive Rs25,000.
evidence.title: PM announces to increase BISP flood relief aid to Rs70b
evidence.excerpt: Sharif said flood relief assistance under BISP would rise from Rs28 billion to Rs70 billion and each affected family would receive Rs25,000.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM announcement carried by the state broadcaster.
contrary_evidence: Emergency cash relief is necessary but temporary.
It does not prove durable income recovery or structural reform.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, describing it as a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient action plan for rehabilitation and reconstruction after the floods.
evidence.title: Prime Minister of Pakistan Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif launches the Resilient, Recovery, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Framework (4RF) for Pakistan Floods
evidence.publisher: Press Information Department, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, describing it as a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient action plan for rehabilitation and reconstruction after the floods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release with explicit PM action and policy framing, but it is self-reporting and not independently audited.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year and tied to the 2022 flood recovery process.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the PM is explicitly named as the launcher and the document says he directed dissemination and stakeholder engagement.
contrary_evidence: The release is about framework launch, not verified implementation or welfare outcomes.
It is a government self-report and needs corroboration from later delivery evidence.

evidence.claim: Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet made up of former rivals, and the cabinet included five women while Miftah Ismail was given the finance portfolio to stabilize the economy.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new PM picks coalition cabinet after Khan ousted
evidence.excerpt: Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet made up of former rivals, and the cabinet included five women while Miftah Ismail was given the finance portfolio to stabilize the economy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters feed on the cabinet formation is reliable for the fact of a coalition cabinet and the named composition, though it is still a news report rather than an official gazette.
evidence.period_fit: Within the target year at the start of the Sharif government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Shehbaz Sharif as prime minister assembling the cabinet, though coalition bargaining constrained selection.
contrary_evidence: Coalition composition is not the same as integrity, and some posts still reflected party bargaining.
This source is more context than proof of ethical restraint.

evidence.claim: Sharif presented the first budget of a coalition government and said the government chose difficult reforms rather than early elections because it wanted to restore the economy and move the country back on track.
evidence.title: Budget Speech 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Sharif presented the first budget of a coalition government and said the government chose difficult reforms rather than early elections because it wanted to restore the economy and move the country back on track.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech with the prime minister's framing of the government's governing choice and priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: this is Sharif's own budget speech as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: The speech is self-justifying and not an independent assessment of success.
It states intent and strategic choice more clearly than implementation results.

evidence.claim: Sharif said the government would prioritize economic stability, support middle and poor households, raise domestic production and agriculture, and improve exports and ease of doing business.
evidence.title: Budget Speech 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Sharif said the government would prioritize economic stability, support middle and poor households, raise domestic production and agriculture, and improve exports and ease of doing business.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech with a clear policy program and target groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the statement is Sharif's own policy framing in office.
contrary_evidence: This is a declared program, not proof of delivery.
The speech also blames the predecessor government, so some of the framing is adversarial.

evidence.claim: The government said it had implemented a Rs2,000 monthly cash transfer for families with income below Rs40,000 from June 2022 and would add about 60 million more people to BISP.
evidence.title: Budget Speech 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The government said it had implemented a Rs2,000 monthly cash transfer for families with income below Rs40,000 from June 2022 and would add about 60 million more people to BISP.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech with a specific cash-transfer policy, start date, and scale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Sharif as prime minister announcing and incorporating the measure into the coalition budget.
contrary_evidence: The claim is programmatic and self-reported, not an independent disbursement audit.
It reflects relief and cushioning more than broad productivity reform.

evidence.claim: The budget raised BISP funding from Rs250 billion to Rs364 billion, projected access for nine million families under Kafalat, expanded educational scholarships to 10 million students, extended Nashonuma nutrition coverage, and increased Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal support for the poor.
evidence.title: Budget in Brief 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The budget raised BISP funding from Rs250 billion to Rs364 billion, projected access for nine million families under Kafalat, expanded educational scholarships to 10 million students, extended Nashonuma nutrition coverage, and increased Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal support for the poor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget summary with explicit allocations and beneficiary targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared but meaningful: this is the federal budget under Sharif's premiership, though delivery would depend on implementing agencies.
contrary_evidence: Allocated amounts and target counts do not prove actual completion in 2022.
These are social-protection commitments inside a fiscally stressed budget.

evidence.claim: The budget framework defined BISP's goal as a nationwide safety net with effective and transparent targeting and delivery mechanisms, and tied it to concrete outputs including unconditional cash transfers, emergency cash transfers, Waseela-e-Taleem, NSER, and Nashonuma.
evidence.title: Performance Based Budget FY 2022-23 to 2024-25
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The budget framework defined BISP's goal as a nationwide safety net with effective and transparent targeting and delivery mechanisms, and tied it to concrete outputs including unconditional cash transfers, emergency cash transfers, Waseela-e-Taleem, NSER, and Nashonuma.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary performance-budget document that links funding to goals and named delivery mechanisms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared attribution: this is a federal performance-budget architecture under Sharif's government, not a personal PM audit of each program arm.
contrary_evidence: This shows institutional design more than realized outcomes.
Performance targets can be aspirational rather than achieved.

evidence.claim: The Public Sector Development Programme was presented as the main instrument for improving socio-economic conditions and achieving government targets, with the 2022-23 budget laying out PSDP size and special packages and relief.
evidence.title: Budget in Brief 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The Public Sector Development Programme was presented as the main instrument for improving socio-economic conditions and achieving government targets, with the 2022-23 budget laying out PSDP size and special packages and relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget document explicitly linking PSDP to government targets and social-economic goals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the PSDP framework is a government choice under Sharif, though execution would sit with multiple ministries and provinces.
contrary_evidence: The document explains planning, not completed implementation.
Large development allocations do not ensure project delivery under crisis conditions.

evidence.claim: Finance Minister Miftah Ismail said Pakistan would cut expenditures and development funds and do belt tightening to revive the IMF programme.
evidence.title: Pakistan to cut expenditures, development funds to revive IMF programme
evidence.excerpt: Finance Minister Miftah Ismail said Pakistan would cut expenditures and development funds and do belt tightening to revive the IMF programme.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete fiscal-adaptation decision is strong and specific, even when syndicated through a secondary site.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but real: this reflects the Sharif government's economic response through its finance minister.
contrary_evidence: Cutting development funds can also indicate weakness or austerity under duress.
The statement is about intended fiscal correction, not guaranteed recovery.
